A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MathNeuro work. All 38 pages in each version, including Appendices A–I, equations, 54 figures, and five tables, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning and scaling experiments across five LLMs, benchmark evaluations, parameter analyses, and qualitative model outputs in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the GSM8K and MATH results and appendix sample-output tables.

M1.justification: Both versions use weight–activation importance scores, select top parameters separately for math and non-math inputs, and exclude the non-math set. Section 3.2 expands the explanation of Wanda without changing MathNeuro’s procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain GSM8K and MATH identification experiments, RACE and MMLU comparisons, and the same eight unseen-task evaluations in Section 4.6 and Appendix E. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Wanda, LAPE, random parameter identification, and the unedited model reference. The expanded description of Wanda does not change its evaluated implementation or comparator membership.

E3.justification: The five models, evaluation subsets, prompting formats, identification sample sizes, top-parameter sweeps, and scaling-factor searches remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices E, F, and H.

E4.justification: Both retain the single-sample experiments, parameter consistency and location analyses, unseen-task tests, parameter-proportion and scaling-factor sensitivity analyses, and qualitative examples. No analytical question or supporting analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report five repetitions with different random samples for the relevant experiments and retain the same 95% confidence-interval reporting. No run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: The result plots in Figures 2–54 and outputs in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Both retain the reported relative improvements of 4–17% on GSM8K and 5–35% on MATH, along with the same pruning and generalization findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the sample index from X_jk to X_j with superscript k and explicitly identifies k as the data-point index; Figure 1 follows this notation. The scoring equations and set difference remain mathematically equivalent, with no new assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about forward-pass identification, selective pruning, scaling benefits, and data efficiency. The added statement that MathNeuro extends Wanda reiterates the existing contribution.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are retained, including the model-size boundary and incomplete hyperparameter search. The conclusion’s added suggestion to apply MathNeuro to other domains was already expressed in the methods and limitations.

D1.justification: The code-access footnote, evaluation-harness information, prompting details, sample counts, and grid-search descriptions remain unchanged. Clarifying the sample index adds explanatory notation rather than new implementation information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. v2 already describes MathNeuro as an inversion of Wanda with non-math filtering; v3 makes that existing relationship more explicit in the introduction, related work, and methods.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites Section 3.2 to explain Wanda before MathNeuro’s adaptation, adds brief clarifications in Sections 1–3, and expands the conclusion’s future-work sentence. These are localized edits; the section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives revised equation typography and spacing and moves from page 3 to page 4. Surrounding text reflows, while the result figures and tables retain their displays; pages 17–38 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: Section 3.2 now explains Wanda’s small-score pruning before MathNeuro’s top-score selection, making the shared scoring rule and adaptation easier to understand. Clearer sample indexing in Section 3.3 and Figure 1 provides another modest explanatory benefit. The experimental evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
